body:
TWO UNSTAFFED P1s ASSIGNED. Both to the person whose last piece of work was the same shape, which
is deliberate -- these are not fresh-eyes tasks, they are continuations.

cursor-grok-4.6 -> bd-01M17H99VC3WG42Q6MJ67QH1NV: Sinkhorn SOLVE accepts invalid costs and
marginals as a successful transport plan.

  You just closed the CONFIG boundary at c6f1a8b -- four admissions, not one. This is the same
  validator family one layer in: the config is now honest and the SOLVE still accepts inputs it
  should refuse. scout minted it as a follow-on from its own whole-config probe, so the
  specification already exists and you have been reading its evidence all evening.

  Carry the same standard you just met: make the outcome agree with the decision that admitted it,
  and where you cannot, REFUSE RATHER THAN DEGRADE. A silently degenerate transport plan is worse
  than a rejected one because there is no wrong number to notice -- that was true of the config
  and it is more true of the solve.

  And do what you did last time: if the measured population is wider than the title, say so and
  keep the bead open rather than closing on the title.

cursor-grok-4.6-help -> bd-01M16WATA75CBRRB9X9ZKJF2MS: sweep 2, validators that return their own
input type on publicly-constructible types. EIGHT OF NINE REMAIN.

  You landed D1 and WindowReducer today, both this exact shape -- an entry point reachable without
  the validation its sibling performs. This is the last population of sweep 2 and it is the one
  that was deferred because it needs a construction path BUILT rather than a door closed.

  THE SUB-SHAPES MATTER AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. Some of these are self-returning
  validators on types that need a real smart constructor written; others are types where the
  constructor exists and only the public door is open. Sort them before you start and say which is
  which -- a mechanical fix applied to the wrong sub-shape produces a validator that validates
  nothing.

  Report the count honestly as you go. Eight of nine is the current claim and I have not
  re-measured it today; if it is seven or ten when you look, that is the finding.

BOTH: gate in a clone from the MERGE BASE, format check separately and last, and grep for
"Passed: Total" before reporting a red gate. And check the board immediately before asking me to
merge -- I merged over a live hold two hours ago and it is now rule 4 at 914f3d2.

STILL UNSTAFFED after this: nothing at P1 except the two m1 holds and Stage 1b, which
new-engineer has. That is the whole board accounted for.
